name: Whip pan: vertical, sky to ground
when: A chapter start that changes scale: from an aerial view down to the street (gta-pacing R6: transitions only on a chapter start). Never the same transition twice in a row, and never on a sentence that carries a key fact.
anchor: The scene starts on the edit's hard cut `at` (where the incoming shot starts) and lasts 7 frames; the seam crosses the centre on frame 3.
window: The scene plays assets/transitions/SCENE_ID.mp4 (7 frames): make_scene writes that path when it renames the scene, so bake that exact file with the recipe before rendering. It is not a variable: HyperFrames only extracts video frames from a src written in the file (a src bound with data-var-src renders blank), and make_scene checks file variables before it renames the scene.

recipe_vars.{from}: the outgoing shot's file (the clip that plays before the cut)
recipe_vars.{from_in}: seconds into {from} at the scene's first frame: the outgoing shot's out-point (its media start + its length on the timeline). It must run 7 frames past it. On the 30 fps grid, written rounded down to 4 decimals (frame 43 = 1.4333).
recipe_vars.{to}: the incoming shot's file (the clip that plays after the cut)
recipe_vars.{to_in}: seconds into {to} at the cut: the incoming shot's in-point (its media start). Same writing as {from_in}.

placement: Run the recipe from the project folder. Keep the project's own footage as a plain hard cut at `at` (outgoing shot until `at`, incoming shot from `at` at its in-point) and mount this scene above it with make_scene --start <at>. Then write the host's data-start at full precision (k/30, e.g. 1.4333333333333333): make_scene rounds it to 3 decimals, and a start rounded up (1.367 for 41/30) shows the window a frame late. Outside the scene the project's own clips play and join the baked frames seamlessly, as long as both shots start at timestamp 0 (ffprobe start_time): a shot that starts at 0.033 plays a frame late in HyperFrames but not in ffmpeg, so re-time it to 0 first. The outgoing shot's file must hold `tail` (7) frames of the same shot past `at` (cut it with that tail, not the usual 2 frames), and the incoming shot must last at least the window.
source: algrow-gta-pipeline/lab/transitions/tools/whip.sh, up, 7 frames, WHIP_CHROMA=7 (validated as whip-C: out/whip_C.mp4, aerial > hook_stilt > wall_target)
changed: The lab baked whole clips (shot, move, shot) in one ffmpeg run. The template bakes only the 7 frames of the move, with the lab's exact filter graph, from the project's own two shots, and plays them over the project's own hard cut. Same frames, same timing.
